label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.

findings.quote: I flagged it ready for its lock. Deck put the title slide in front of it.
findings.why: The chapter opens in the team's private shorthand (flagged, lock, parts) before any of it is explained, which a phone reader in a gap between meetings will skim past.

findings.quote: Dev had built the tool to do it that afternoon.
findings.why: Lock is used from here on and only defined at line 45, after the scene that depends on it.

findings.quote: The team was racing its own locks, and the locks lost.
findings.why: A reporter's verdict with no I and no hindsight, and it is said again at line 118.

findings.quote: its own locks lost the race
findings.why: Repeats the line at 37 and the same hold-versus-locks point already made at 49 and 63.

findings.quote: That is the point of diminishing returns, and it is the moment to stop.
findings.why: This is the best takeaway in the chapter, but it comes as a 'That is the point' opening followed by two short sentences.

findings.quote: four hundred and thirty-nine commits by the agents, a hundred and sixty-two sessions
findings.why: The conductor reads out the tally in words and a Figure card at line 91 then shows it again; a busy reader gets numbers with no use for them.

findings.quote: It was used once. Anyone on the team could stop everything
findings.why: A run of three short sentences closes the chapter; and 'only I could start it again' is the thing a team copying this most needs, so it deserves a longer sentence.

findings.quote: There was one thing we did not have, and stopping was the only safe move without it.
findings.why: Teases a miss that chapter 17 opens by saying again, so the reader is told twice and given the substance only in the second.

findings.quote: Chapter 16 told this one. In a line:
findings.why: The lock card retells chapter 16 and then two Dev lines (32, 34) retell it a third time.

findings.quote: In the night I froze the slides, and five minutes later the researcher sent a correction
findings.why: The freeze and the five-minutes-late correction are told in chapter 7 (line 99) and here in near-identical terms.

findings.quote: Not a disaster on stage. A small, true error that the record caught
findings.why: Short fragments in a row where one running sentence would carry the thought.

findings.quote: it was nothing sensitive, an agent that got a bit excited
findings.why: A team weighing this pattern wants to know what stopped data leaving other sites' pages; the shrug undercuts a failure the chapter says stays in at full size.

findings.quote: The failures stay in, at full size.
findings.why: Nearly the same sentence as line 5, within a screen of it.

findings.quote: By two in the morning the team had a clock and a hold.
findings.why: Wake, clock and hold are all used as known things in the opening; wake record is only defined at line 19.

findings.quote: Good. But know what it is:
findings.why: An instruction on how to take the line, spoken by the conductor in a way that reads as the book instructing the reader.

what_holds: 17-what-did-not-work.md: each miss gets a card with its cost and whose record says so, and the key-in-a-log card gives a response to copy (rotate first, report, do not hide it); that is a takeaway I could use tomorrow.

07-hour-three-the-five-steps.md: the five stages are plain (plan, check the plan, do, check the work, check against plan), the record that fails the gate is a pattern I could copy with my own agents, and 'Partial is a true answer' is memorable.
16-hour-nineteen-minute-by-minute.md: the hold file and its one rule ('No member lifts it'), plus the finding that a hold stops the next session, not the one running, answer how it stops.
notes: As a team lead I worry about the deal-breaker of one central person: in all three sections the conductor and the editor are the hub (only the editor lifts the hold, the conductor routes everything), and the sections do not say how a team without that hub would copy it. Chapter 16 is the weakest for a 5-minute phone read because its first half is insider shorthand and its tally is not tied to a takeaway until line 109. The Something to try boxes are short and usable.
